principle: Use source-backed details when present. When the source is silent, require a documented, context-appropriate Indian visual convention or an explicit artistic approval; never declare one regional, historical or sectarian style canonical for every Purana or era.

subject_gates.subject: HELMETS_AND_CROWNS
required_checks: not used as generic good-versus-evil coding

explicit_foreign_style_exclusions.label: Trojan, Spartan or Odyssey-style battle equipment
unsupported fantasy emblem on a flag
European castle architecture without source justification

dm04_specific_failures.finding: An Asura warrior wears red-crested Greco-Roman-looking headgear. The crest wording in the character proposal did not authorize a Roman, Hellenistic, Trojan or Spartan silhouette.
dm04_specific_failures.future_rule: Do not use a transverse or longitudinal Greco-Roman plume, Corinthian face form or classical Mediterranean armor vocabulary. Source silence must remain source silence until a documented Indian convention is reviewed.

dm04_specific_failures.finding: A black/red demonic-face flag emblem appears without demonstrated source or tradition support.
dm04_specific_failures.future_rule: Use no faction emblem when none is sourced or artistically approved; a plain story-appropriate standard is still a proposal and must be labeled SOURCE_SILENT.

source_silence_protocol: Offer one or more documented, context-appropriate Indian visual conventions as proposals, with region, medium and uncertainty named.
Require ARTISTICALLY_APPROVED before an exact design becomes reusable.
Never describe an approved proposal as scriptural fact or universal canon.
fail_closed_rules: Any FORBIDDEN element produces FIX or ESCALATE, never PASS.
A sacred-identity conflict produces ESCALATE unless the correction is unambiguous and source-backed.
A visually attractive image cannot pass if source, iconography or cultural-authenticity evidence fails.
Only an image-capable independent reviewer may make semantic pixel conclusions.
